title.narrative: Strong (women) smallholders and CSAs of Nepal’s western mountain regions for a resilient local food system (EMPOWER)

description.narrative: Nepal’s mountain food system faces severe challenges due to loss of agrobiodiversity, out-migration, feminization of agriculture, low productivity, and growing climate risks. Poor diets, gender barriers, and weak local solutions further limit resilience.Target Group & Area: 2,000 households in three municipalities of Bajura and Mugu.Overall Objective: Empower women smallholders and CSAs to build resilient local food systems. Key Outputs:Enhanced capacities on agrobiodiversity, climate-resilient, and nutrition-sensitive practices.Strengthened local markets for safe and nutritious foods.Empowered CSAs and networks advocate for the right to food. Partners: LI-BIRD, KCDC, FWEAN.

Overall Objectives: Empowered women smallholders, marginalized communities and civil society actors strengthen resilient local food systems.Project Objective/ Outcome1,600 women smallholders and youth from targeted municipalities adopt agroecology-based farming practices and civil society actors and local authorities promote agroecological principles and practices to enhance local agrobiodiversity and strengthen food, nutrition and income security.Indicator: At least 70% (1,120) of the targeted 1,600 households meet an acceptable food consumption score by end of the project60% of targeted households report increased crop diversity and annual cash income by end of the project. Two targeted local governments have developed and endorsed appropriate policies and guidelines and have increased their annual fiscal budget by 10% for the promotion of agroecology-based food production and green esterprises by end of the project.

Project Area: Budinanda (Bajura) and Khatyad (Mugu) municipalities, Sudurpaschim and Karnali provinces.Direct Target Groups:1,600 smallholder households; priority to women-headed, marginalized, climate-affected, low-income households; ≥70% women participation.20 local government representatives for planning, implementation, and monitoring capacity building.80 extension workers for technical support and sustainability.60+ community-based organizations and 2 policy networks for advocacy and institutional support.Indirect Target Groups:38,904 people benefiting via trained extension workers.1,000 urban and semi-urban consumers benefiting from campaigns and local food products.Total Reach: Over 40,000 individuals indirectly and ~9,000 directly.
